inspirations.feedback_summary:
Concept is physically plausible and COTS-buildable in kind - 4x rigid grouser wheels, front transverse drum, central hopper on rear mast, 24 V bus, sealed box, sensor mast, dual radio - no conservation, load-path or signal-path violation. RASSOR prior art does not invalidate it: single drum loses counter-rotating cancellation but 45.7 N reaction vs ~400-500 N weight gives traction ratio >5, and separate hopper + mast to 1.05 m adds tip moment and spill path but is ordinary Earth-gravity engineering, unlike RASSOR drum-as-hopper Z-stand.
Re-derivation decides the vote: 341 W x 0.5 h = 171 Wh, not 1000 Wh. 1000 Wh / 2.92 kg = 342 Wh/kg pack. Everyday scale: LiFePO4 cells ~120-140 Wh/kg, pack ~90-110 Wh/kg; laptop NMC pack ~200-250 Wh/kg cells; 342 Wh/kg LiFePO4 pack is outside everyday scale by ~3x. Either energy is ~0.17-0.3 kWh and 2.92 kg is roughly right for NMC / light LiFePO4, or energy is 1 kWh and mass should be ~8-10 kg. Even corrected, 50.6 -2.92 +~9 = ~57 kg still under 60 kg, so likely closable, but not closed. Lift energy 2400 J E60 vs 15 kg x 9.81 x 1.05 m = ~155 J useful implies 15x overhead - model, friction or time-window error to check. 10 kg at 900 kg/m3 = 0.0111 m3 E49 is correct vs 0.00625 m3 E44 error, ~11 L bucket ~ person-size carry-on, plausible. 4.06 tip factor with 0.30 m overhang vs 7.1 earlier shows moment-arm sensitivity vs wheelbarrow experience - geometry must be fixed.
Key claims resting on no evidence/source: actuator force with friction through linkage (E56 failed), runtime from pack at full load (E59 failed, E58 failed), dimensioned stowed 1.0x0.5x0.5 m envelope with 300 mm wheels + stowed 900 mm mast + 1050 mm hopper travel (sketches E11/E46/E57 show deployed topology only, E22/E45 failed), sealed-box 22 K rise E53 and 0.00332 m3/s for 80 W E52 are closed but IP65 dust claim has only generic search E27-E29, no seal/detail. Contact/torque/cutting E10, power E34, sensor power E47, hopper volume E49, stopping distance E21 have calc/simulate support.
Meeting facts: closed by cycle cap without consensus, v2 by Sam, 1 ready (Mara) to 3 not-ready (Theo, Priya, Sam). Blocking O1 mass integration, O2 dump kinematics/tip, O4 battery mass-energy all point to same two missing proofs. In my judgement those objections are sound and leave the concept unsettled - not fundamentally unworkable, but buildable not proven on sound analysis. Hence not accept yet; on resubmittal with the two recomputes above and a stowed envelope sketch, this should be accept-ready, with dust/thermal and FPV latency left as test tuning in feedback, not as acceptance blockers.
inspirations.why_useful: Rejected but near-closable integrated rover example; shows how to catch 171Wh vs 1000Wh / 342Wh-per-kg pack error, lift-energy overhead, tip-moment sensitivity, and missing stowed-envelope proof before acceptance.

concepts.text: Locomotion: four rigid wheels with grousers (traction bars), 300 mm diameter x 150 mm wide. Analogy: farm tractor and Mars rover wheels - large diameter spreads weight, grousers bite loose soil.
concepts.author: Mara — Excavation and Mobility Engineer

concepts.text: Excavator: front transverse rotating drum (bucket-wheel style, RASSOR analogy) 200 mm dia x 400 mm wide, shallow cut 30 mm, lifts soil into central hopper. Alternative: drag blade. Drum chosen for continuous cut and low shock.
concepts.author: Mara — Excavation and Mobility Engineer

concepts.text: Folding perception mast: two First Person View (FPV) cameras plus depth sensor and Inertial Measurement Unit (IMU) on folding mast, stowed flat under 0.5 m, deployed to ~1.0 m for view over hopper and drum. Analogy: sailboat mast and periscope - low stow, high eye.
concepts.author: Theo — Autonomy and Remote Operations Engineer

concepts.text: Heartbeat stop-and-hold teleoperation: 5 GHz WiFi link with heartbeat monitor, onboard compute hold-to-run autonomy, Emergency Stop (E-stop) latching stop-and-hold on link loss or latency exceedance. Analogy: industrial Automated Guided Vehicle (AGV) deadman switch.
concepts.author: Theo — Autonomy and Remote Operations Engineer

concepts.text: Rear high-lift mast hopper dump: hopper pivot 0.45 m stowed rising to 1.05 m pour lip (0.60 m rise) via 0.15 m stroke dual actuators through 4-to-1 chain at 0.80 friction efficiency. Analogy forklift mast.

evidence.output_full:
Light cold-box ground versus wind loads — from 20261102-112524_off-grid-solar-powered-cold-storage-for-
A tonne of produce spread over a few square metres imposes only ~2.5 kPa floor and soil pressure, an order of magnitude below typical allowable soil bearing of tens to >50 kPa, so bearing rarely governs lightweight cold stores. Lateral wind governs anchoring: dynamic pressure follows ~0.6 x V^2, or ~540 Pa at 30 m/s gust, yielding ~2.9 kN on a ~5 m2 side wall that must be carried by anchors, plinth fixings and separate PV supports.
Evidence: E47 (soil pressure under plinth without concrete self-weight: 2.51 kPa); E48 (floor loading from produce alone: 2.45 kPa); E64 (wind pressure at 30 m/s gust: 540 Pa); E65 (wind force on side wall: 2.86×10³ N); E43 (search: concrete slab soil bearing capacity kPa small building foundation: spaworld.co.nz — Generic Concrete Slab or Pad Building Guide | Portable Spas — https://www.spaworld.co.nz/learn/how-to-build-a-generic-concrete-slab-or-pad-for-a-portable-spa-pool/); E44 (search: concrete slab soil bearing capacity kPa small building foundation: amcfoam.com — Revised: March 2010 — 2010 — https://amcfoam.com/PDFs/Normal%20and%20Problem%20Soils.pdf)

evidence.output_full:
ISO 11228-2 single-operator push-pull envelope — from 20261102-105608_stair-climbing-hand-truck-for-parcel-cou
ISO 11228-2 and HSE guidance limit sustained one-person push-pull to roughly 200-250 N with brief heave below ~350 N using closed-loop grips at ~90-110 cm height. A 60 kg load dragged continuously up a stair slope needs ~441 N, exceeding the envelope; stepwise levered lifts in the ~226 N class or powered assist are needed to comply.
Evidence: E7 (search: EN ISO hand truck safety standard 60 kg push pull force limits: mktg.idec.com — ISO 11228-2? — https://mktg.idec.com/hubfs/EU_AWD/AWD_ISO-11228-2.pdf?hsLang=en); E8 (search: EN ISO hand truck safety standard 60 kg push pull force limits: webarchive.nationalarchives.gov.uk — Microsoft Word - updated version of report 9648.doc — https://webarchive.nationalarchives.gov.uk/ukgwa/20100707143156mp_/http://www.hse.gov.uk/research/rrpdf/rr228.pdf); E12 (search: ISO 11228-2 push pull force limits ergonomics handles: mktg.idec.com — AWD ISO 11228 2.pdf — https://mktg.idec.com/hubfs/EU_AWD/AWD_ISO-11228-2.pdf?hsLang=fr); E58 (stair heave lever effort brake torque tip margin 60kg: W=706.3N angle=38.7deg Fslope=441N Flever=226N T=98.9Nm Tsf=197.8Nm tip=21.8deg lean=25.0 margin=-3.2; energy per 0.2m riser=141J vs daily ~)

Light cold-box ground versus wind loads — from 20261102-112524_off-grid-solar-powered-cold-storage-for-
A tonne of produce spread over a few square metres imposes only ~2.5 kPa floor and soil pressure, an order of magnitude below typical allowable soil bearing of tens to >50 kPa, so bearing rarely governs lightweight cold stores. Lateral wind governs anchoring: dynamic pressure follows ~0.6 x V^2, or ~540 Pa at 30 m/s gust, yielding ~2.9 kN on a ~5 m2 side wall that must be carried by anchors, plinth fixings and separate PV supports.
Evidence: E47 (soil pressure under plinth without concrete self-weight: 2.51 kPa); E48 (floor loading from produce alone: 2.45 kPa); E64 (wind pressure at 30 m/s gust: 540 Pa); E65 (wind force on side wall: 2.86×10³ N); E43 (search: concrete slab soil bearing capacity kPa small building foundation: spaworld.co.nz — Generic Concrete Slab or Pad Building Guide | Portable Spas — https://www.spaworld.co.nz/learn/how-to-build-a-generic-concrete-slab-or-pad-for-a-portable-spa-pool/); E44 (search: concrete slab soil bearing capacity kPa small building foundation: amcfoam.com — Revised: March 2010 — 2010 — https://amcfoam.com/PDFs/Normal%20and%20Problem%20Soils.pdf)

Pedestrian crowd resonant force model — from 20261102-121628_vibration-retrofit-for-a-lively-pedestri
Vertical walking force is modeled as ~700 N body weight with ~280 N (~40%) first harmonic at step resonance. Sparse walkers add linearly, but dense crowd Class III ~0.5 pedestrians/m2 uses imperfect synchronization: equivalent in-phase count Neq ~ 10.8*sqrt(zeta*N) acting together at resonance, producing kN-scale harmonic force and multi-m/s2 bare-deck acceleration when structural damping is ~0.5-1%.
Evidence: E41 (search: Setra footbridge crowd load density synchronized pedestrians equivalent number: mdpi.com — Vibration Serviceability Assessment of a Historic Suspension Footbridge — http://mdpi.com/2075-5309/12/6/732/htm); E42 (search: Setra footbridge crowd load density synchronized pedestrians equivalent number: 1library.net — 4.4.1 Dynamic load cases - Footbridge guide setra — https://1library.net/article/dynamic-load-cases-footbridge-guide-setra.ye693erq); E44 (search: Eurocode pedestrian vertical force harmonic walking frequency: eurocodes.jrc.ec.europa.eu — Microsoft Word - Geradin_JRC_Design of Footbridges_150909.doc — 2021 — https://eurocodes.jrc.ec.europa.eu/sites/default/files/2021-12/jrc_53442.pdf); E49 (equivalent synchronized pedestrians dense crowd: 5.29); E50 (dense crowd resonant force from equivalent pedestrians: 1.48e+03)
